prior_findings.nsenter_waiter: Successful start/swap records actual private worker; guarded signal_worker validates immutable worker, current identity/argv and pidfd. Actual CPU namespace test asserts distinct waiter/worker and ends old worker.
prior_findings.mapped_uid: require_owner_view accepts exact original or one-level map, retains PID/start/boot/private namespace identity and rejects changed map. Actual kernel mapped-owner test present. quiet/release remain host-only unchanged.
prior_findings.finite_effects: ContextVar callback checks fresh deadline/intent/control/private signed LINE service permission before main spawn/signal/wait paths; try/finally reset and no legacy callback are tested. Remaining exception noted below.
prior_findings.action_scope: _bound and effect_guard explicitly reverify launch_workorder + external WO/driver/profile/service_action=line_stack_restart; ReadSnapshot preserves read-only use inside write fence.

adoption_review: Initial serve uses actual source/nonce/agent/run state + submit intent/context and existing from_native adoption; then confirms unique native ID and caller descendant of pinned Fabro. No new blocker identified in this bounded read-only review. Host vs inner API selection requires pinned root/profile/hash/netns holder identity; actual own namespace test present.

findings.problem: On health timeout, proc.kill() is unguarded and signals the nsenter host waiter instead of actual managed private-PID worker. Worker can survive the failed serve and retain GPU memory.
findings.minimal_repair: When serving is supplied, capture exact worker and signal_worker through fresh guard; preserve legacy cleanup for servingNone. Prove an actual CPU private worker with wrong health/model is gone while foreign worker stays alive; no model/GPU qualification claimed.
